before.statement:

Write $\lambda_j\cdot z$ for the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] on $\mathbb R^n$ and $e^{iw}$ for the complex exponential of [[def-complex-exponential]] at $iw$, and consider the $\mathbb C^q$-valued map $F(z):=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\,e^{i\lambda_j\cdot z}$ on $U$. Then: (a) [Complex independence] if $F(z)=0$ for every $z\in U$, then $c_1=\dots=c_m=0$. (b) [Real-part grouping rule] if $\operatorname{Re}F(z)=0$ for every $z\in U$, then for every $
u\in\mathbb R^n$ the grouped coefficient $$C_
u:=\sum_{\lambda_j=
u} c_j+\sum_{\lambda_j=-

(c) [Scope] no hypothesis beyond pairwise distinctness of the $\lambda_j$ and nonemptiness and openness of $U$ is used; $\lambda_j=0$ is allowed and the $\lambda_j$ need not be nonzero, ordered or normalized. before.title: The two-equation interface admittance system: solution formulas and the normal-flux identity
before.statement:
Let $Y_1,Y_2\in\mathbb C$ with $Y_1+Y_2
e0$, and let $E_i,E_r,E_t\in\mathbb C$ satisfy the two linear equations $$E_i+E_r=E_t,\qquad Y_1(E_i-E_r)=Y_2E_t.$$ Then: (a) [Solution] If $E_i
e0$, then $$r:= rac{E_r}{E_i}= rac{Y_1-Y_2}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad t:= rac{E_t}{E_i}= rac{2Y_1}{Y_1+Y_2};$$ if $E_i=0$ then $E_r=E_t=0$ and the ratios are undefined. (b) [Normal-flux identity] If $Y_1>0$ is real (the incident side admittance), then $$|r|^2+ rac{\operatorname{Re}Y_2}{Y_1}\,|t|^2=1,$$ and explicitly $|t|^2=\dfrac{4Y_1^2}{|Y_1+Y_2|^2}$ and $|r|^2=1-\dfrac{4Y_1\operatorname{Re}Y_2}{|Y_1+Y_2|^2}$. The second summand $(\operatorname{Re}Y_2/Y_1)|t|^2$ is nonnegative if and only if $\operatorname{Re}Y_2\ge0$; it is the normal-flux coefficient of a passive transmitted medium and may be negative for an active one, in which case $|r|>1$ and the identity carries no energy-conservation reading. (c) [Pure-imaginary admittance] If $Y_1>0$ is real and $Y_2$ is purely imaginary, then $|r|=1$, $\operatorname{Re}Y_2\,|t|^2=0$ and $|t|^2=\dfrac{4Y_1^2}{Y_1^2+|Y_2|^2}>0$; in particular $r
e0$ and $t
e0$. (d) [Real-positive specialisation] If $Y_1,Y_2>0$ are real, then $r=(Y_1-Y_2)/(Y_1+Y_2)$ and $t=2Y_1/(Y_1+Y_2)$ are real and $|r|^2+(Y_2/Y_1)|t|^2=1$; with $Y_j=1/Z_j$, $Z_j>0$, this is $r=(Z_2-Z_1)/(Z_1+Z_2)$, $t=2Z_2/(Z_1+Z_2)$ and $R+T=1$ for $R=|r|^2$, $T=(Z_1/Z_2)|t|^2$, in agreement with [[lem-em-interface-wave-linear-system]]. (e) [Scope] The lemma is pure algebra of $\mathbb C$; the labels 'incident', 'reflected' and 'transmitted' and the interpretation of the second summand as a flux fraction belong to the consuming physical theorem, not to this lemma.
before.strategy:
Part (a): substitute $E_r=E_t-E_i$ (from the first equation) into the second: $Y_1(2E_i-E_t)=Y_2E_t$, i.e. $2Y_1E_i=(Y_1+Y_2)E_t$; since $Y_1+Y_2
e0$ this gives $E_t=2Y_1E_i/(Y_1+Y_2)$, and then $E_r=E_t-E_i=(Y_1-Y_2)E_i/(Y_1+Y_2)$ ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]], field arithmetic [[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]]). If $E_i
e0$ the two ratios are the displayed $r$ and $t$; if $E_i=0$ both $E_r$ and $E_t$ vanish and no ratio is defined. Part (b): use $|z|^2=z\overline z$ and the binomial identity $|Y_1+Y_2|^2-|Y_1-Y_2|^2=4\operatorname{Re}(Y_1\overline{Y_2})$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]): for real $Y_1>0$ the right side is $4Y_1\operatorname{Re}Y_2$, so $|r|^2=|Y_1-Y_2|^2/|Y_1+Y_2|^2=1-4Y_1\operatorname{Re}Y_2/|Y_1+Y_2|^2$ while $|t|^2=4Y_1^2/|Y_1+Y_2|^2$; adding $(\operatorname{Re}Y_2/Y_1)|t|^2$ cancels the correction term and yields the asserted identity. The sign and active-medium remarks follow from $|r|^2\ge0$ and $|r|>1\iff\operatorname{Re}Y_2<0$ whenever $|t|>0$. Part (c): for $Y_2=i eta$, $ eta\in\mathbb R$, and real $Y_1>0$ one has $\overline{Y_1+Y_2}=Y_1-Y_2$, hence $|r|=|Y_1-Y_2|/|Y_1+Y_2|=1$, and the identity of (b) gives $\operatorname{Re}Y_2\,|t|^2=0$; moreover $Y_1+Y_2
e0$ because $Y_1>0$, so $|t|^2=4Y_1^2/(Y_1^2+ eta^2)>0$. Part (d): substituting $Y_j=1/Z_j$ with $Z_j>0$ into (a) gives $r=(1/Z_1-1/Z_2)/(1/Z_1+1/Z_2)=(Z_2-Z_1)/(Z_1+Z_2)$ and $t=2Z_2/(Z_1+Z_2)$, and (b) gives $|r|^2+(Z_1/Z_2)|t|^2=1$, i.e. $R+T=1$ for the stated $R,T$. All divisions are by nonzero complex numbers; no choice principle is used. ∎

Consider a declared region with vanishing free charge density and no external free current, so that $ho_f=0$ and the free current is the conduction current $J_f=\sigma E$. Let $k\in\mathbb C^{3}$, $\omega>0$ and $e,h\in\mathbb C^{3}$, and for $(x,t)\in\mathbb R^{3}	imes\mathbb R$ define $E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re} igl(e\,e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)} igr)$ and $H(x,t):=\operatorname{Re} igl(h\,e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)} igr)$ componentwise, i.e. with the phase convention $e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}$ and the real-part encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]; put $D:=\varepsilon E$, $B:=\mu H$ and $J_f:=\sigma E$. Extend the Euclidean inner and cross products to $\mathbb C^{3}$ by the same componentwise polynomial formulas ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]). Then: (a) [Exact propagation constant and decay] $\lambda^{2}=k\cdot k=\varepsilon\mu\omega^{2}+i\mu\sigma\omega=a+ib$, so $\lambda=\pm(p+iq)$; if $x_3':=n\cdot x$, then for $\lambda=p+iq$ $$E(x,t)=e^{-q x_3'}\,\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e\,e^{i(p x_3'-\omega t)}\bigr),$$ so the field oscillates with wavenumber $p$ and its amplitude decays in the direction of increasing $x_3'$ at the exact rate $q$; with $\lambda=-(p+iq)$ the same formula holds with $e^{q x_3'}$, which grows in that direction, so the decaying branch is the one with $\lambda=p+iq$, in agreement with the selection rule of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]](b). (d) [Poor-conductor regime] put $t':=b/a=\sigma/(\varepsilon\omega)>0$. For every $t'\le1/2$ the exact value satisfies $$\Bigl|q-\frac{\sigma}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\varepsilon}}\Bigr|\le\frac{t'^{2}}{4}\cdot\frac{\sigma}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\varepsilon}},\qquad\Bigl|\delta-\frac{2}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon}{\mu}}\Bigr|\le\frac{t'^{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon}{\mu}},$$ so in this regime $\delta$ is frequency-independent up to the displayed relative error $O\bigl((\sigma/(\varepsilon\omega))^{2}\bigr)$. after.statement: Assume the elementary inertial-rest branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] in the isotropic scalar case at rest in the laboratory frame with constants $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ and $\sigma>0$, the fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and the plane-wave structure of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]]: let $\omega>0$, $e\in\mathbb C^{3}\setminus\{0\}$, $n$ a unit vector and $k=\lambda n$, $\lambda\in\mathbb C$, and let $E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e\,e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}\bigr)$ be a plane-wave field satisfying the amplitude conditions of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](b) with $k\cdot e=0$. Put $a:=\mu\varepsilon\omega^{2}>0$, $b:=\mu\sigma\omega>0$, $r:=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}$ and let $p,q>0$ be the quantities of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]. Then: (a) [Exact propagation constant and decay] $\lambda^{2}=k\cdot k=\varepsilon\mu\omega^{2}+i\mu\sigma\omega=a+ib$, so $\lambda=\pm(p+iq)$; if $x_3':=n\cdot x$, then for $\lambda=p+iq$ $$E(x,t)=e^{-q x_3'}\,\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e\,e^{i(p x_3'-\omega t)}\bigr),$$ so the field oscillates with wavenumber $p$ and its amplitude decays in the direction of increasing $x_3'$ at the exact rate $q$; with $\lambda=-(p+iq)$ the exact formula is $E(x,t)=e^{q x_3'}\operatorname{Re}(e\,e^{i(-p x_3'-\omega t)})$, which grows in that direction, so the decaying branch is the one with $\lambda=p+iq$, in agreement with the selection rule of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]](b). (b) [Exact skin depth] $q^{2}=\bigl(\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}-a\bigr)/2$, $p^{2}=\bigl(\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}+a\bigr)/2$, $pq=b/2=\mu\sigma\omega/2$, and the skin depth of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]] equals the exact closed expression $$\delta(\omega)=\frac{1}{q}=\frac{\sqrt{2\,(r+a)}}{b}=\frac{\sqrt{2\bigl(\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}+a\bigr)}}{\mu\sigma\omega}.$$ (c) [Good-conductor regime] put $t:=a/b=\varepsilon\omega/\sigma>0$. (d) [Poor-conductor regime] put $t':=b/a=\sigma/(\varepsilon\omega)>0$. For every $t'\le1/2$ the exact value satisfies $$\Bigl|q-\frac{\sigma}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\varepsilon}}\Bigr|\le\frac{t'^{2}}{4}\cdot\frac{\sigma}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\varepsilon}},\qquad\Bigl|\delta-\frac{2}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon}{\mu}}\Bigr|\le\frac{t'^{2}}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{\sigma}\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon}{\mu}},$$ so in this regime $\delta$ is frequency-independent up to the displayed relative error $O\bigl((\sigma/(\varepsilon\omega))^{2}\bigr)$. before.title: Normal-incidence amplitudes and the flux budget, with the Ohmic transmitting medium
before.statement: Assume the setting of [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] at normal incidence: medium 1 in $\{x_3<0\}$ with $\varepsilon_1,\mu_1>0$, $\sigma_1=0$, medium 2 in $\{x_3>0\}$ with $\varepsilon_2,\mu_2>0$ and either $\sigma_2=0$ (lossless) or $\sigma_2>0$ (Ohmic), both homogeneous and at rest in the laboratory chart, with the plane interface $S=\{x_3=0\}$ and normal $n=e_3$. Let $\omega_i,\omega_r,\omega_t>0$ and let three plane waves of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] be given with wavevectors $k_i=k_1n$ ($k_1>0$), $k_r=-k_1n$ and $k_t=k\,n$, where for $\sigma_2=0$ one takes $k=\omega_t/v_2>0$ and for $\sigma_2>0$ one takes $k=\kappa_2(\omega_t)=p+iq$ with the complex propagation constant of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]; amplitudes $e_i,e_r,e_t\in\mathbb C^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ and $h_j=k_j\times e_j/(\mu_j\omega_j)$ satisfying the conditions of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](b)-(c) in their media, and the four stationary interface identities of [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] holding on $\mathbb R^{2}\times I$ for a nonempty open interval $I$. Then: (a) [Common frequency] $\omega_i=\omega_r=\omega_t=:\omega$ for some $\omega>0$ ([[pthm-em-phase-matching]](a)). (b) [Amplitude system and solution] all three electric amplitudes are tangential to $S$, and the two tangential interface identities reduce to $$e_i+e_r=e_t,\qquad Y_1\,(e_i-e_r)=Y_2\,e_t,\qquad Y_1:=\frac{k_1}{\mu_1\omega}>0,\qquad Y_2:=\frac{k}{\mu_2\omega};$$ hence $e_r=r\,e_i$ and $e_t=t\,e_i$ with the complex scalars $$r=\frac{Y_1-Y_2}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad t=\frac{2Y_1}{Y_1+Y_2};$$ in particular the reflected and transmitted electric phasors are parallel to the incident one (normal-incidence polarisation preservation), and $r,t\ne0$. (c) [Lossless transmitting medium] if $\sigma_2=0$ then $Y_2=1/Z_2>0$ with $Z_2=\sqrt{\mu_2/\varepsilon_2}$ of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]], so $$r=\frac{Z_2-Z_1}{Z_1+Z_2}\in\mathbb R,\qquad t=\frac{2Z_2}{Z_1+Z_2}\in\mathbb R,$$ in agreement with [[lem-em-interface-wave-linear-system]]; the period-$T$ averaged normal fluxes of the stored-energy model, $T=2\pi/\omega$ ([[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](d), [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]]), are $\langle S_i\cdot n\rangle=\frac{|e_i|^{2}}{2Z_1}$, $\langle S_r\cdot n\rangle=-\frac{|e_r|^{2}}{2Z_1}$ and $\langle S_t\cdot n\rangle=\frac{|e_t|^{2}}{2Z_2}$, and with $R:=r^{2}$, $T:=\frac{Z_1}{Z_2}t^{2}=\frac{4Z_1Z_2}{(Z_1+Z_2)^{2}}$ one has $R+T=1$; $R$ is the reflected and $T$ the transmitted fraction of the incident normal averaged flux. (d) [Ohmic transmitting medium] if $\sigma_2>0$ then $Y_2=\kappa_2(\omega)/(\mu_2\omega)$ has $\operatorname{Re}Y_2=q/(\mu_2\omega)>0$, and $$r=\frac{Y_1-Y_2}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad t=\frac{2Y_1}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad |r|^{2}+\frac{\operatorname{Re}Y_2}{Y_1}\,|t|^{2}=1 .$$ The second summand is the fraction of the incident period-averaged normal flux that enters the conductor at the interface; the transmitted field has the exact decay factor $e^{-qx_3}$ ([[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](c) applied to $k=p+iq$) and, by the Ohmic dissipation clause of [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]], the entering flux is absorbed in the conductor: the reflected fraction $|r|^{2}$ and the absorbed fraction $(\operatorname{Re}Y_2/Y_1)|t|^{2}$ add to $1$. (e) [Scope] no existence or uniqueness of interface-consistent data, no oblique incidence, no anisotropic or dispersive media, no ideal conductor ($\sigma_2=\infty$), no nonlinear response and no empirical claim is made. The interface identities are the stationary plane-interface conditions of the model, supplied for compact interfaces by [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]; the flux identities are the model's stored-energy and Ohmic-dissipation reading, not an observational claim.

after.statement: Assume the following plane-interface material setting, with the same explicitly adopted stationary interface identities as [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] (including its absent-wave qualification), at normal incidence: medium 1 in $\{x_3<0\}$ with $\varepsilon_1,\mu_1>0$, $\sigma_1=0$, medium 2 in $\{x_3>0\}$ with $\varepsilon_2,\mu_2>0$ and either $\sigma_2=0$ (lossless) or $\sigma_2>0$ (Ohmic), both homogeneous and at rest in the laboratory chart, with the plane interface $S=\{x_3=0\}$ and normal $n=e_3$. Let $\omega_i,\omega_r,\omega_t>0$ and let three plane waves of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] be given with wavevectors $k_i=k_1n$ ($k_1>0$), $k_r=-k_1n$ and $k_t=k\,n$, where for $\sigma_2=0$ one takes $k=\omega_t/v_2>0$ and for $\sigma_2>0$ one takes $k=\kappa_2(\omega_t)=p+iq$ with the complex propagation constant of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]; amplitudes $e_i\in\mathbb C^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ and $e_r,e_t\in\mathbb C^{3}$ and $h_j=k_j\times e_j/(\mu_j\omega_j)$ satisfying the conditions of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](b)-(c) in their media, and the four stationary interface identities of [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] holding on $\mathbb R^{2}\times I$ for a nonempty open interval $I$. Then: (a) [Common frequency] The transmitted amplitude is nonzero and $\omega_i=\omega_t=:\omega$ for some $\omega>0$. If $e_r\ne0$, then $\omega_r=\omega$ as well; if $e_r=0$, assign $\omega_r=\omega$ conventionally, since an absent field cannot determine a frequency. Matching is proved directly from the interface characters, so the lossless-only physical scope of [[pthm-em-phase-matching]] is not used to infer the Ohmic branch. (b) [Amplitude system and solution] all three electric amplitudes are tangential to $S$, and the two tangential interface identities reduce to $$e_i+e_r=e_t,\qquad Y_1\,(e_i-e_r)=Y_2\,e_t,\qquad Y_1:=\frac{k_1}{\mu_1\omega}>0,\qquad Y_2:=\frac{k}{\mu_2\omega};$$ hence $e_r=r\,e_i$ and $e_t=t\,e_i$ with the complex scalars $$r=\frac{Y_1-Y_2}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad t=\frac{2Y_1}{Y_1+Y_2};$$ in particular the reflected and transmitted electric phasors are parallel to the incident one (normal-incidence polarisation preservation), and $t\ne0$. The reflection coefficient is zero exactly when $Y_1=Y_2$, in particular at a lossless impedance-matched interface; the zero reflected field remains part of the theorem. (c) [Lossless transmitting medium] if $\sigma_2=0$ then $Y_2=1/Z_2>0$ with $Z_2=\sqrt{\mu_2/\varepsilon_2}$ of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]], so $$r=\frac{Z_2-Z_1}{Z_1+Z_2}\in\mathbb R,\qquad t=\frac{2Z_2}{Z_1+Z_2}\in\mathbb R,$$ in agreement with [[lem-em-interface-wave-linear-system]]; the period-$T$ averaged normal fluxes of the stored-energy model, $T=2\pi/\omega$ ([[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](d), [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]]), are $\langle S_i\cdot n\rangle=\frac{|e_i|^{2}}{2Z_1}$, $\langle S_r\cdot n\rangle=-\frac{|e_r|^{2}}{2Z_1}$ and $\langle S_t\cdot n\rangle=\frac{|e_t|^{2}}{2Z_2}$, and with $R:=r^{2}$, $T:=\frac{Z_1}{Z_2}t^{2}=\frac{4Z_1Z_2}{(Z_1+Z_2)^{2}}$ one has $R+T=1$; $R$ is the reflected and $T$ the transmitted fraction of the incident normal averaged flux. (d) [Ohmic transmitting medium] if $\sigma_2>0$ then $Y_2=\kappa_2(\omega)/(\mu_2\omega)$ has $\operatorname{Re}Y_2=p/(\mu_2\omega)>0$, and $$r=\frac{Y_1-Y_2}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad t=\frac{2Y_1}{Y_1+Y_2},\qquad |r|^{2}+\frac{\operatorname{Re}Y_2}{Y_1}\,|t|^{2}=1 .$$ The second summand is the fraction of the incident period-averaged normal flux that enters the conductor at the interface; the transmitted field has the exact decay factor $e^{-qx_3}$ (the explicit factorization $e^{i(p+iq)x_3}=e^{-qx_3}e^{ipx_3}$) and, by the Ohmic dissipation clause of [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]], the entering flux is absorbed in the conductor: the reflected fraction $|r|^{2}$ and the absorbed fraction $(\operatorname{Re}Y_2/Y_1)|t|^{2}$ add to $1$. (e) [Scope] no existence or uniqueness of interface-consistent data, no oblique incidence, no anisotropic or dispersive media, no ideal conductor ($\sigma_2=\infty$), no nonlinear response and no empirical claim is made. The interface identities are the stationary plane-interface conditions of the model, supplied for compact interfaces by [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]]; the flux identities are the model's stored-energy and Ohmic-dissipation reading, not an observational claim.

after.strategy: Polarisation data: for (s), $e_j=E_j\hat y$ gives $k_j\cdot e_j=E_j(k_j\cdot\hat y)=0$ (because $k_j=\kappa+k_{j3}n$ and $\hat y\perp\kappa,n$); for (p), $e_j=-(k_j\times\hat y)H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ gives $k_j\cdot e_j=0$ as well, and $k_j\times e_j=k_j\times\bigl(-(k_j\times\hat y)H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)\bigr)=H_j\bigl[(k_j\cdot k_j)\hat y-k_j(k_j\cdot\hat y)\bigr]/(\omega\varepsilon_j)=H_j(k_j\cdot k_j)\hat y/(\omega\varepsilon_j)=\omega\mu_jh_j$ using $k_j\cdot k_j=\varepsilon_j\mu_j\omega^{2}$ and $k_j\cdot\hat y=0$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]](b)). So both polarisations satisfy the amplitude conditions in the respective media. (a): with the common interface phase the tangential electric identity is the coefficient identity $e^{\tau}_i+e^{\tau}_r=e^{\tau}_t$ (where $v^{\tau}=v-(v\cdot n)n$); for (s) this is $E_i\hat y+E_r\hat y=E_t\hat y$, i.e. the scalar identity; for (p) the tangential part of $e_j$ is $(e_j\cdot\hat x)\hat x$ because $e_j$ lies in $\operatorname{span}\{\kappa,n\}$ (as $k_j\times\hat y\perp\hat y$ and $k_j\in\operatorname{span}\{\kappa,n\}$), so the identity is $E^{(p)}_i+E^{(p)}_r=E^{(p)}_t$. The tangential magnetic identity $n\times h_i+n\times h_r=n\times h_t$ similarly becomes, after taking components in the fixed direction and expressing $h_j$ through the electric amplitude: for (s), $h_j=(k_j\times e_j)/(\mu_j\omega)$ has tangential component in the $\hat\kappa$-direction equal to $-k_{j3}E_j/(\mu_j\omega)$ (the reflected sign included, since $k_{r3}=-k_{13}$), which yields $Y^{s}_1(E^{s}_i-E^{s}_r)=Y^{s}_2E^{s}_t$ with $Y^s_1=k_{13}/(\mu_1\omega)$, $Y^s_2=k_{t3}/(\mu_2\omega)$; for (p), $e_j=-(k_j\times\hat y)H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ has $\hat\kappa$-component $k_{j3}H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ and the magnetic identity $H_i+H_r=H_t$ gives, after expressing $H_j$ in the amplitudes, $Y^{p}_1(E^{p}_i-E^{p}_r)=Y^{p}_2E^{p}_t$ with $Y^p_1=\varepsilon_1\omega/k_{13}$, $Y^p_2=\varepsilon_2\omega/k_{t3}$ for $k_{t3}\ne0$; both are instances of the two-equation system of [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]], whose clause (a) gives the displayed $r_\chi,t_\chi$ (the determinant $Y^{\chi}_1+Y^{\chi}_2$ is nonzero in each branch: in the propagating branch both are real positive, in the evanescent branch the real part of the sum is $Y^{\chi}_1>0$). (b): the real-propagation statement is [[pthm-em-phase-matching]](c) applied with the common $(\kappa,\omega)$; The admittance magnitudes $Y_1^s=k_{13}/(\mu_1\omega)$, $Y_1^p=\varepsilon_1\omega/k_{13}$, $Y_2^s=k_{t3}/(\mu_2\omega)$ and $Y_2^p=\varepsilon_2\omega/k_{t3}$ are real and positive because $k_{13}>0$ and $k_{t3}>0$. The reflected signed normal component is $k_{r3}=-k_{13}$, so its normal-flux coefficient is $-Y_1^\chi$, not a positive admittance. The flux identities are clauses (d),(e) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]]: for (s) the normal flux of wave $j$ is $|e_j|^{2}k_{j3}/(2\mu_j\omega)=(k_{j3}/(\mu_j\omega))|E_j^s|^2/2$, giving respectively $+Y_1^s|E_i^s|^2/2$, $-Y_1^s|E_r^s|^2/2$ and $+Y_2^s|E_t^s|^2/2$; for (p), $E_j^p=k_{j3}H_j/(\omega\varepsilon_j)$ and the normal flux is $k_{j3}|H_j|^2/(2\omega\varepsilon_j)=(\varepsilon_j\omega/k_{j3})|E_j^p|^2/2$. The latter coefficient is negative for the reflected wave; writing it as $-Y_1^p$ gives the signed reflected flux. Thus both polarisations use $+Y_1$ for incidence and $-Y_1$ for reflection, and $+Y_2$ for transmission. Substituting the amplitudes gives $R_\chi+T_\chi=1$ by [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]](b) with the real positive magnitudes $Y_1^\chi,Y_2^\chi$. (c): Away from the critical TM branch, the finite-admittance formula gives $r_\chi=0$ exactly for $Y_1^\chi=Y_2^\chi$. For equal permeabilities and unequal positive indices, equality of TE admittances would imply $k_{13}=k_{t3}$ and hence $K_1=K_2$, impossible. The TM equality is $n_1\cos\theta_t=n_2\cos\theta_i$ together with Snell $n_1\sin\theta_i=n_2\sin\theta_t$. Squaring and eliminating $\sin\theta_t$ gives $(n_1^2-n_2^2)[n_2^2-(n_1^2+n_2^2)\sin^2\theta_i]=0$. For unequal indices divide only by the nonzero first factor to obtain $\sin^2\theta_i=n_2^2/(n_1^2+n_2^2)$ and $\tan\theta_i=n_2/n_1$; strict monotonicity of tangent on $(0,\pi/2)$ gives uniqueness, and $\sin\theta_t=n_1/\sqrt{n_1^2+n_2^2}<1$ proves admissibility. For equal indices and permeabilities the two media are identical: Snell gives $\theta_t=\theta_i$, both admittances agree at every allowed angle, and $r_s=r_p=0$, $t_s=t_p=1$. No uniqueness inference follows in that degenerate branch. (d): for $|\kappa|>K_2$ the selection $k_{t3}=i\beta$ gives $Y^{s}_2=k_{t3}/(\mu_2\omega)=i\beta/(\mu_2\omega)$ and $Y^{p}_2=\varepsilon_2\omega/(i\beta)=-i\varepsilon_2\omega/\beta$, both purely imaginary ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]); clause (c) of [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]] gives $|r_\chi|=1$ and $|t_\chi|^{2}=4(Y^{\chi}_1)^{2}/((Y^{\chi}_1)^{2}+|Y^{\chi}_2|^{2})>0$; the transmitted field structure, decay and normal-flux vanishing are clause (e) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] applied to the transverse polarisations (the (s) case is the $e$ polarisation $n'\times\hat\kappa_0$ with $n'=n$, $\kappa_0=\kappa$; the (p) case is the corresponding $h$ polarisation). The reflected flux equals the incident flux because $|r_\chi|=1$. (e): At critical incidence solve without defining $Y_2^p$. The TE equations have $Y_2^s=0$, so $E_r^s=E_i^s$ and $E_t^s=2E_i^s$, giving $r_s=1$, $t_s=2$. For TM, $E_i^p=k_{13}H_i/(\omega\varepsilon_1)$, $E_r^p=-k_{13}H_r/(\omega\varepsilon_1)$ and $E_t^p=0$. The electric boundary identity forces $H_r=H_i$; the magnetic one gives $H_t=H_i+H_r=2H_i$. Thus $r_p=-1$, $t_p=0$ as ratios of the nonzero incident tangential electric amplitude. The transmitted electric vector is $-\kappa\times\hat y\,H_t/(\omega\varepsilon_2)$, a normal vector that need not vanish. Both transmitted normal fluxes are zero by direct $\operatorname{Re}(e_t\times\overline h_t)\cdot n/2$ calculation (or the real-wave normal factor $k_{t3}=0$). The four interface identities are consistent: the normal D jump for TM reduces to $H_t=H_i+H_r$, and the normal B jump for TE to $E_t^s=E_i^s+E_r^s$. All critical conclusions are therefore established by finite equations. (f) is a scope statement. All divisions are by nonzero complex numbers; no choice principle is used. ∎

before.statement: Adopt the isotropic scalar Ohmic branch of [[post-em-material-closure]] at rest and the exact quantities of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]] and [[pthm-em-conducting-skin-depth]]. Let the declared parameters be $$\varepsilon=4\ \mathrm F\,\mathrm m^{-1},\qquad \mu=1\ \mathrm H\,\mathrm m^{-1},\qquad \sigma=100\ \mathrm S\,\mathrm m^{-1},\qquad \omega=3\ \mathrm s^{-1};$$ these are declared model parameters of the illustration, not measured values of any material. Then: (i) $a=\mu\varepsilon\omega^{2}=36$, $b=\mu\sigma\omega=300$, $r=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}=\sqrt{91296}$ and $t=a/b=3/25=0.12\le1/4$, so the good-conductor regime of [[pthm-em-conducting-skin-depth]](c) applies; (ii) the exact propagation and attenuation constants are $p=\sqrt{(r+36)/2}$ and $q=\sqrt{(r-36)/2}$, with $pq=b/2=150$ exactly; the decimal evaluations $r\approx302.15228$, $p\approx13.00293$, $q\approx11.53586$ satisfy $q<\sqrt{b/2}=\sqrt{150}\approx12.24745$ with $$|q-\sqrt{150}|\approx0.71159\le 2t\sqrt{150}=0.24\sqrt{150}\approx2.93939,$$ and for the skin depth $\delta=1/q\approx0.08669$ against $\sqrt{2/b}=1/\sqrt{150}\approx0.08165$ one has $$|\delta-\sqrt{2/b}|\approx0.00504\le 4t\sqrt{2/b}=0.48\sqrt{2/b}\approx0.03919 .$$ Thus the exact skin depth satisfies the stated good-conductor bound with the margin predicted by the theorem. (iii) for $\sigma=0$ (same $\varepsilon,\mu,\omega$) one has $b=0$, $q=0$, no attenuation and $\delta=+\infty$ by the convention of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]](c); the inequalities of (ii) do not apply, consistently with the exclusion recorded in [[pthm-em-conducting-skin-depth]](f). (iv) [Scope] the computation is an exact check of the stated inequalities for the declared dimensionless data; it reports no measurement, no material identification and no empirical claim, and the decimal evaluations are displayed only as approximate illustrations of the exact expressions.
before.strategy: Direct substitution in the theorem: $a=\mu\varepsilon\omega^{2}=1\cdot4\cdot9=36$ and $b=\mu\sigma\omega=1\cdot100\cdot3=300$; $r=\sqrt{36^{2}+300^{2}}=\sqrt{1296+90000}=\sqrt{91296}$; $t=36/300=3/25$; $pq=\sqrt{(r^{2}-a^{2})/4}=b/2=150$ by the exact identity of [[pthm-em-conducting-skin-depth]](b). The two inequalities are the displayed bounds of that theorem specialised to $t=3/25$; the decimal values are rounded evaluations of the exact radicals, computed as $r=\sqrt{91296}$, $q=\sqrt{(r-36)/2}$, $\delta=1/q$, and displayed to five decimals. The $\sigma=0$ clause is the convention $\delta=+\infty$ of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]](c) together with $q=0$ at $b=0$. No empirical input or measurement enters.

before.title: The Brewster angle at an equal-permeability interface and the surviving $s$-reflection
before.statement: Adopt the setting of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]] with two lossless media at rest, equal permeabilities $\mu_1=\mu_2=:\mu>0$ and declared refractive indices $n_1=1$, $n_2=3/2$ (declared model parameters, not optical measurements), so that $\varepsilon_j=n_j^{2}/(c^{2}\mu)$ and $K_j=n_j\omega/c$ in the notation of [[def-em-medium-wave-parameters]]. Then: (i) [Brewster angle] by [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]](c) the TM amplitude vanishes exactly at the unique angle $\theta_B\in(0,\pi/2)$ with $\tan\theta_B=n_2/n_1=3/2$, i.e. $\sin\theta_B=3/\sqrt{13}$, $\cos\theta_B=2/\sqrt{13}$; the transmitted angle satisfies $n_1\sin\theta_B=n_2\sin\theta_t$, hence $\sin\theta_t=2/\sqrt{13}$, and $\theta_B+\theta_t=\pi/2$; (ii) [Amplitudes] at $\theta_i=\theta_B$ one has $Y^{p}_1=Y^{p}_2=\sqrt{13}/(2c\mu)$, hence $r_p=0$ and $t_p=1$; the remaining $s$-amplitudes are $Y^{s}_1=2/(\sqrt{13}c\mu)$, $Y^{s}_2=9/(2\sqrt{13}c\mu)$ and $$r_s=\frac{2/\sqrt{13}-9/(2\sqrt{13})}{2/\sqrt{13}+9/(2\sqrt{13})}=-\frac{5}{13},\qquad t_s=\frac{8}{13};$$ (iii) [Flux budget] with $R_s=|r_s|^{2}=25/169$ and $T_s=(Y^{s}_2/Y^{s}_1)|t_s|^{2}=(9/4)(64/169)=144/169$ one has $R_s+T_s=169/169=1$ exactly, while the TM channel has $R_p=0$, $T_p=1$; (iv) [Scope] the numbers are declared model parameters; the example is a deterministic computation of the classical interface model, reports no measurement, and the statement that the reflected beam is TM-polarised at the Brewster angle concerns exactly the TM channel of this idealisation (an unpolarised incident beam is not modelled here).
before.strategy: Substitution in [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]]: $K_j=n_j\omega/c$ and the admittances are $Y^{s}_j=k_{j3}/(\mu\omega)$, $Y^{p}_j=\varepsilon_j\omega/k_{j3}$ with $k_{13}=(\omega/c)\cos\theta_B=(2/\sqrt{13})(\omega/c)$ and, at $\theta_t$ with $\sin\theta_t=2/\sqrt{13}$, $k_{t3}=(3\omega/(2c))(3/\sqrt{13})=(9/(2\sqrt{13}))(\omega/c)$; hence $Y^{s}_1=2/(\sqrt{13}c\mu)$, $Y^{s}_2=(9/4)Y^{s}_1=9/(2\sqrt{13}c\mu)$ and $Y^{p}_1=\varepsilon_1\omega/k_{13}=\sqrt{13}/(2c\mu)=Y^{p}_2$ (the equality $Y^{p}_1=Y^{p}_2$ is exactly the Brewster condition of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]](c) and gives $r_p=(Y^{p}_1-Y^{p}_2)/(Y^{p}_1+Y^{p}_2)=0$, $t_p=1$). The $s$-amplitudes follow from the admittance formulas of that theorem by factoring $1/(\sqrt{13}c\mu)$ from numerator and denominator: $r_s=(4/2-9/2)/(4/2+9/2)=-5/13$ and $t_s=2\cdot(4/2)/(13/2)=8/13$; the flux identities are clause (b) of the same theorem: $T_s=(Y^{s}_2/Y^{s}_1)|t_s|^{2}=(9/4)\cdot(64/169)=144/169$, and $25/169+144/169=1$ exactly. The angles: $\sin\theta_t=n_1\sin\theta_B/n_2=(2/3)(3/\sqrt{13})=2/\sqrt{13}=\cos\theta_B$ gives $\theta_B+\theta_t=\pi/2$. All numbers are exact rational or quadratic-irrational expressions; no empirical input, no measurement and no statistical claim is used.

Excluded: measured refractive indices, absorption, interfaces between unequal permeabilities, unpolarised-beam statistics and every empirical claim.

before.title: Total internal reflection: decaying transmitted field, vanishing normal flux and the reflection phase
before.statement: Adopt the setting of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]] with equal permeabilities $\mu_1=\mu_2=:\mu>0$ and declared indices $n_1=3/2$, $n_2=1$ (declared model parameters, not measurements), and the transverse-electric polarisation $e_j=E_j\hat y$. Let the incidence angle be given by $\sin\theta_i=4/5$, which exceeds the critical angle $\theta_c$ with $\sin\theta_c=n_2/n_1=2/3$, so $|\kappa|=K_1\sin\theta_i=(6/5)(\omega/c)>(\omega/c)=K_2$. Then with $\beta=\sqrt{|\kappa|^{2}-K_2^{2}}=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$ and $k_{13}=(\omega/c)(3/2)(3/5)=(9/10)(\omega/c)$: (i) [Reflection] $Y^{s}_1=9/(10\mu c)$, $Y^{s}_2=i\sqrt{11}/(5\mu c)$ and $$r_s=\frac{9/10-i\sqrt{11}/5}{9/10+i\sqrt{11}/5},\qquad |r_s|=1,\qquad t_s=\frac{9/5}{9/10+i\sqrt{11}/5},\qquad |t_s|^{2}=\frac{324}{125};$$ the reflection factor is the phase $r_s=e^{-2i\varphi}$ with $\varphi=\arctan\!\bigl(2\sqrt{11}/9\bigr)\approx0.63525$ (about $36.40^\circ$), i.e. the reflected wave acquires the phase $-2\varphi\approx-1.2705$ (about $-72.79^\circ$); (ii) [Transmitted field] the transmitted field is $E_t(x,t)=e^{-\beta x_3}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(E_t\hat y\,e^{i(\kappa x_1-\omega t)}\bigr)$ with $\beta=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$: it decays by the factor $e^{-\sqrt{11}/5}\approx0.51514$ when $x_3$ increases by $c/\omega$, its period-averaged normal flux vanishes identically, $\langle S_t\cdot n\rangle\equiv0$, while its tangential averaged flux is positive, $\langle S_t\cdot\hat\kappa\rangle=e^{-2\beta x_3}\,\frac{(6/5)(\omega/c)|E_t|^{2}}{2\mu\omega}=e^{-2\beta x_3}\frac{3|E_t|^{2}}{5\mu c}$; (iii) [Flux budget] $|r_s|^{2}+(\operatorname{Re}Y^{s}_2/Y^{s}_1)|t_s|^{2}=1+0=1$, so the whole incident normal averaged flux is reflected, while the evanescent field carries a tangential averaged flux only; (iv) [Scope] the example is an exact deterministic computation of the lossless interface model for declared parameters; it reports no measurement, and the presence of a tangential evanescent flux is not a claim about information speed or signal propagation.
before.strategy: Substitution in [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]](d): $K_1=(3/2)(\omega/c)$, $\kappa=K_1\sin\theta_i=(6/5)(\omega/c)$, $\beta=\sqrt{(36/25-1)}(\omega/c)=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$, $k_{13}=K_1\cos\theta_i=(3/2)(3/5)(\omega/c)$ (because $\cos\theta_i=3/5$), so $Y^{s}_1=k_{13}/(\mu\omega)=9/(10\mu c)$ and $Y^{s}_2=i\beta/(\mu\omega)=i\sqrt{11}/(5\mu c)$. Then $r_s=(Y^{s}_1-Y^{s}_2)/(Y^{s}_1+Y^{s}_2)$, whose numerator is the complex conjugate of its denominator, so $|r_s|=1$; $|t_s|^{2}=|2Y^{s}_1|^{2}/|Y^{s}_1+Y^{s}_2|^{2}=(81/25)/(81/100+11/25)=324/125$ by [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws|the modulus laws]]; the phase is the argument of the denominator and satisfies $\tan\varphi=(\sqrt{11}/5)/(9/10)=2\sqrt{11}/9$, hence $r_s=e^{-2i\varphi}$. The decay and normal-flux vanishing are clause (e) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] with $n'=n$, $\kappa_0=\kappa$ and the transverse-electric polarisation; the tangential-flux value is its displayed formula $|\kappa_0||e|^{2}/(2\mu\omega)=|\kappa||E_t|^{2}/(2\mu\omega)$ with $|\kappa|=(6/5)(\omega/c)$. The flux budget is clause (d) of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]] with $\operatorname{Re}Y^{s}_2=0$. The decimal values are rounded evaluations of the exact expressions $\arctan(2\sqrt{11}/9)$ and $e^{-\sqrt{11}/5}$. No empirical input is used.

Excluded: measured indices, absorption, information-speed or signal-propagation claims, and every empirical statement.

after.statement: Adopt the setting of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]] with equal permeabilities $\mu_1=\mu_2=:\mu>0$ and declared indices $n_1=3/2$, $n_2=1$ (declared model parameters, not measurements), choose the tangential wavevector $\kappa=(6\omega/(5c))e_1$, so $\hat\kappa=e_1$ and $\hat y=n\times\hat\kappa=e_2$, and take the transverse-electric polarisation $e_j=E_j\hat y$. Let the incidence angle be given by $\sin\theta_i=4/5$, which exceeds the critical angle $\theta_c$ with $\sin\theta_c=n_2/n_1=2/3$, so $|\kappa|=K_1\sin\theta_i=(6/5)(\omega/c)>(\omega/c)=K_2$. Then with $\beta=\sqrt{|\kappa|^{2}-K_2^{2}}=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$ and $k_{13}=(\omega/c)(3/2)(3/5)=(9/10)(\omega/c)$: (i) [Reflection] $Y^{s}_1=9/(10\mu c)$, $Y^{s}_2=i\sqrt{11}/(5\mu c)$ and $$r_s=\frac{9/10-i\sqrt{11}/5}{9/10+i\sqrt{11}/5},\qquad |r_s|=1,\qquad t_s=\frac{9/5}{9/10+i\sqrt{11}/5},\qquad |t_s|^{2}=\frac{324}{125};$$ the reflection factor is the phase $r_s=e^{-2i\varphi}$ with $\varphi=\arctan\!\bigl(2\sqrt{11}/9\bigr)\approx0.63514703$ (about $36.39124^\circ$), i.e. the reflected wave acquires the phase $-2\varphi\approx-1.27029406$ (about $-72.78249^\circ$); (ii) [Transmitted field] the transmitted field is $E_t(x,t)=e^{-\beta x_3}\operatorname{Re}\bigl(E_t\hat y\,e^{i(|\kappa|x_1-\omega t)}\bigr)$ with $\beta=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$: it decays by the factor $e^{-\sqrt{11}/5}\approx0.51514$ when $x_3$ increases by $c/\omega$, its period-averaged normal flux vanishes identically, $\langle S_t\cdot n\rangle\equiv0$, while its tangential averaged flux is positive, $\langle S_t\cdot\hat\kappa\rangle=e^{-2\beta x_3}\,\frac{(6/5)(\omega/c)|E_t|^{2}}{2\mu\omega}=e^{-2\beta x_3}\frac{3|E_t|^{2}}{5\mu c}$; (iii) [Flux budget] $|r_s|^{2}+(\operatorname{Re}Y^{s}_2/Y^{s}_1)|t_s|^{2}=1+0=1$, so the whole incident normal averaged flux is reflected, while the evanescent field carries a tangential averaged flux only; (iv) [Scope] the example is an exact deterministic computation of the lossless interface model for declared parameters; it reports no measurement, and the presence of a tangential evanescent flux is not a claim about information speed or signal propagation.
after.strategy: Substitution in [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]](d): $K_1=(3/2)(\omega/c)$, $\kappa=(6\omega/(5c))e_1$, $|\kappa|=K_1\sin\theta_i=(6/5)(\omega/c)$, $\hat\kappa=e_1$ and $\hat y=e_2$, $\beta=\sqrt{(36/25-1)}(\omega/c)=(\sqrt{11}/5)(\omega/c)$, $k_{13}=K_1\cos\theta_i=(3/2)(3/5)(\omega/c)$ (because $\cos\theta_i=3/5$), so $Y^{s}_1=k_{13}/(\mu\omega)=9/(10\mu c)$ and $Y^{s}_2=i\beta/(\mu\omega)=i\sqrt{11}/(5\mu c)$. Then $r_s=(Y^{s}_1-Y^{s}_2)/(Y^{s}_1+Y^{s}_2)$, whose numerator is the complex conjugate of its denominator, so $|r_s|=1$; $|t_s|^{2}=|2Y^{s}_1|^{2}/|Y^{s}_1+Y^{s}_2|^{2}=(81/25)/(81/100+11/25)=324/125$ by [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws|the modulus laws]]; the phase is the argument of the denominator and satisfies $\tan\varphi=(\sqrt{11}/5)/(9/10)=2\sqrt{11}/9$, hence $r_s=e^{-2i\varphi}$. The decay and normal-flux vanishing are clause (e) of [[pthm-em-medium-plane-wave-fields]] with $n'=n$, $\kappa_0=\kappa$ and the transverse-electric polarisation; the tangential-flux value is its displayed formula $|\kappa_0||e|^{2}/(2\mu\omega)=|\kappa||E_t|^{2}/(2\mu\omega)$ with $|\kappa|=(6/5)(\omega/c)$. The flux budget is clause (d) of [[pthm-em-oblique-fresnel]] with $\operatorname{Re}Y^{s}_2=0$. The decimal values are rounded evaluations of the exact expressions $\arctan(2\sqrt{11}/9)$ and $e^{-\sqrt{11}/5}$. No empirical input is used.
after.physical_scope: Deterministic example of total internal reflection in the lossless interface model for declared indices $n_1=3/2$, $n_2=1$ at $\sin\theta_i=4/5$: the unit-modulus reflection factor with its phase, the evanescent transmitted field with decay factor $e^{-\beta x_3}$, the vanishing normal and positive tangential averaged fluxes. Excluded: measured indices, absorption, information-speed or signal-propagation claims, and every empirical statement.
